assumptions: Standard 11x11 base-game layout version 2, Golems at tier 5; no mods.
Actual world-layout selection loaded from game source; private export appended only in the in-memory analysis module.
Proposed five-candidate pool: uniform count 1..5, uniform subset, area-weighted integer bills. Radius weights .75,.875,1,1.125,1.25 are an analysis assumption; equal-area sensitivity also run.
Every newly opened map is visited immediately. Discovered unfinished hole maps block unexplored orthogonal neighbors from all approaches. Existing explored maps and Roads remain available.
No resource depletion in the main experiment; one explicit Home depletion stress case is separate.
Road edges are adjacent-map links, not local cables. Clearing does not remove map nodes.

PRIMARY online policies know only revealed terrain and costs. They search for a Lake at reachable tiers <=3 and a Dwarven source at tiers <=6, then approach the four known corner coordinates. They do not know encounter locations, hidden bills or the seed layout. Extended play searches nearer unknown cells until finding all four Golems. Endpoint access does not prove factory completion.

Direct online play searches nearer frontier first, then commits to random monotone corner routes. Adaptive online play avoids known clearing bills during source search, then replans shortest corner paths using revealed blocker costs, with unknown terrain priced at zero. Both clear all discovered neighboring blockers before each newly opened cell.

After surveying, both online policies share shortest routes on the revealed map, trying 16 terminal orders. Every corner route achieves its exact 10-hop Manhattan lower bound. Total shared network optimization is heuristic, not a certified global Steiner optimum.

SUPPLEMENTARY oracle/legacy corridor policies know source locations, and oracle also knows hidden terrain/budgets; excluded from the main recommendation after the user specified no distribution knowledge.
Affordability, factory production, local routing, travel/UI overhead, Core unlock timing and wall-clock completion are not simulated. No save injection or accelerated game run.

Gross Stone availability assumes every opened ordinary map reserve is accessible, with no factory consumption or mining loss. It is an optimistic accounting screen only; guarded camp access and infinite Golem production are excluded.
Core item bags assume one initial Exploration purchase (5 Simple + 5 Basic), one free destination and subsequent current destination quotes; omitted from progression timing.
